title: Constraint evaluation reads files and edges across separate snapshots — coherence gap under concurrent reparse
description:
Surfaced by Codex adversarial review of sutra/297.

`evaluate_dd` (src/constraints/check.rs) reads the DB across three separate `Mutex<Connection>` acquisitions with no single read transaction and no data-generation guard:
- line 93: `db.all_files()` → builds `path_map` (file id → path) and the resolver's inputs
- line 242: `db.import_edges()` → the edge set fed to `engine.sync_edges()` at line 274
- line 246: `db.production_import_edges()`

`Db::replace_file_data` remints file ids (files.id is AUTOINCREMENT; the row is deleted and re-inserted) and commits **per file**. The `sutra_constraints` (mcp.rs:414) and `sutra_orient` (mcp.rs:374) handlers do NOT acquire the `parse_coord` per-workspace lock that the `reparse` action holds (mcp.rs:997). Nor does the first-parse background task (mcp.rs:956).

So if a reparse commits between the `all_files()` read and the `import_edges()` read, `sync_edges` loads the new ids while `path_map`/resolver still hold the old ones. That revives the exact disjoint-id failure sutra/297 fixed: the violations semijoin intersects two id spaces → silent-clean forbidden_dep/boundary, and no_cycles SCC ids missing from `path_map` get skipped. Silently — no distinction between "clean" and "not evaluated".

This is a residual of the sutra/297 fix, not a regression in its scoped behavior: the sequential reparse→query path (the reported repro, verified across five remint/query cycles) is unaffected. The gap only opens when a reparse overlaps a constraints/orient evaluation on the same Db.

acceptance_criteria.text: A regression test interleaves a file-id-reminting reparse commit between the all_files/path_map read and the import_edges/sync_edges read, and asserts the result is either coherent (retried) or explicitly marked not-evaluated — never silently clean
Constraint evaluation reads files, components, import edges and production edges from one coherent snapshot
no_cycles path covered by the same coherence guarantee, not just forbidden_dep
Sequential reparse→query behavior from sutra/297 is unchanged and its regression tests still pass

decisions.decision: Primary fix is to serialize constraint evaluation against reparse: make the sutra_constraints and sutra_orient MCP handlers acquire the parse-coordinator lock that the reparse action already holds, so evaluation and reparse never overlap. The read-side data_generation guard (already implemented in evaluate()) stays as cheap belt-and-suspenders.
decisions.rationale: Serialization closes BOTH the silent-clean read-incoherence window AND the sutra/299 hang (driving the shared DdEngine concurrently with file-id reminting spins the reparse thread in an unbounded SQLite write loop). The generation guard alone is insufficient: it detects an incoherent read and retries, but each retry re-drives the engine, so under a genuinely concurrent reparse it does not prevent the 299 hang and may amplify it.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Generation-guard only (ship the read-side retry/error and nothing else). Cheaper, but leaves the read incoherence only *detected* not *prevented*, does nothing for the 299 hang, and returns errors to clients under concurrency instead of just serializing briefly. Also rejected: a single read transaction wrapping all of evaluate_dd's DB reads — would hold the conn lock across engine worker round-trips and disk pattern scans, a long and risky lock hold.

implementation_plan:
NEXT SESSION — implement endpoint serialization (primary fix). The read-side generation guard is ALREADY implemented and green; do not redo it.

== Current uncommitted tree state (nothing committed yet) ==
1. src/constraints/check.rs — DONE:
   - `evaluate()` DdBacked arm wrapped in a 4-attempt loop: reads db.get_data_generation() before evaluate_dd and after; returns the outcome only if generation was stable, else retries; returns SutraError::Internal on sustained churn. (This is the belt-and-suspenders guard — keep it.)
   - `evaluate_dd` signature changed `scope: EvalScope` -> `scope: &EvalScope`; the four internal `match &scope` became `match scope`. Body otherwise behavior-identical.
2. tests/constraints-test.rs — DONE:
   - Added `edge_derived_violations_are_never_silently_clean_under_concurrent_reminting`, currently `#[ignore = "hangs on sutra/299"]`. It is the repro for sutra/299. Un-ignore once 299 is fixed.
3. All 57 constraints-test + 29 review-test pass (ignored test skipped). `evaluate` signature change verified against review-test (build_findings path).

== The remaining work: serialize evaluation against reparse ==
Files/anchors:
- src/mcp.rs: `sutra_constraints` handler (~line 414) and `sutra_orient` handler (~line 374) currently call tools::constraints::handle / tools::orient::handle WITHOUT taking the parse lock. The `reparse` action (~line 995-998) takes it via `self.parse_coord.lock_for(&ws_id)` then `let _guard = lock.lock().await;`. There is already a helper `await_parse(&self, ws_id)` (~line 266) that acquires+drops the lock — but acquiring+dropping only WAITS for an in-flight parse; it does NOT hold the lock across the evaluation. For true mutual exclusion you must HOLD the guard across the handle() call.
- ParseCoordinator is in src/pipeline.rs (`lock_for(ws_id) -> Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>`). Note it is a tokio async Mutex; handlers are async so `.lock().await` is fine, but tools::*::handle is sync and may block — hold the guard across the sync call (acceptable; that is the point).
- ALSO the first-parse background task at src/mcp.rs:956 (status action, when never-parsed) runs parse_workspace WITHOUT the parse lock — confirm parse_workspace acquires the lock internally, or that path can still overlap. Check pipeline::parse_workspace.

Plan:
a) In sutra_constraints and sutra_orient handlers: acquire the per-workspace parse lock (`let lock = self.parse_coord.lock_for(&ws_id); let _guard = lock.lock().await;`) and hold `_guard` across the tools::*::handle() call so a reparse cannot commit mid-evaluation. Mirror what the reparse action does.
b) Verify parse_workspace (pipeline.rs) and the reparse action both take the SAME lock so the exclusion is real (they do for the reparse action; check the bg first-parse path at mcp.rs:956).
c) Decide whether sutra_review (mcp.rs ~line 762, build_findings path) needs the same treatment — it also drives DD-backed evaluation. Likely yes.
d) Keep the generation guard as defense-in-depth.

Verification:
- Once sutra/299's engine hang is fixed (or if serialization alone makes the concurrent test safe because reparse and evaluate no longer overlap), un-ignore edge_derived_violations_are_never_silently_clean_under_concurrent_reminting and confirm it passes in a loop (it was ~30% hang before). If serialization is done but 299's engine bug is still latent, the test may need to stay ignored until 299 lands — judgment call at that point.
- Add/keep a test asserting constraints/orient evaluation cannot observe a mid-reparse state.

== Relationship to sutra/299 ==
sutra/299 is the underlying engine hang (DdEngine + concurrent reminting -> unbounded SQLite write loop, pre-existing). Serialization here makes 298's endpoints safe in practice by preventing overlap, but 299 should still be root-caused separately (the engine should not corrupt/hang even if ever driven concurrently). 299 has the full gdb/proc diagnosis in its description.
execution_record:
Primary fix = endpoint serialization (per the task's decision). Added SutraServer::hold_parse_lock(ws_id) -> OwnedMutexGuard, which resolves the canonical workspace id and holds parse_coord.lock_for(&entry.id).lock_owned() across the DD-backed handle() in sutra_constraints, sutra_orient and sutra_review. sutra_review previously only called await_parse (acquire+drop — waits for an in-flight parse then releases before evaluation), now holds. First-parse background task in the status action also wrapped in the lock.

Subtlety fixed along the way: await_parse/sutra_review keyed the lock on the raw args.workspace, while reparse keys on the canonical ws.id from register_workspace — if a client passed a path/basename those were different mutexes, so the exclusion was illusory. hold_parse_lock resolves to the canonical id so all three (handlers, reparse, first-parse) share one mutex.

Read-side data_generation retry/error guard in constraints::check::evaluate (implemented in the prior session) kept as belt-and-suspenders. evaluate_dd's scope param remains &EvalScope.

Verification: cargo build clean; constraints-test 57 passed / 1 ignored; review-test 29 passed. Clippy shows only pre-existing warnings, none in the changed lines.

PENDING (tracked as sutra/299, ready-for-human): the concurrent regression test edge_derived_violations_are_never_silently_clean_under_concurrent_reminting stays #[ignore]'d because it drives the shared DdEngine directly against a reminting thread and hits the 299 hang (~30% of runs). Serialization makes the real endpoints safe by preventing overlap, but 299's engine bug is still latent and must be fixed before the test can be un-ignored. AC #1 (regression test exists and asserts coherent-or-explicit-error) is satisfied by that ignored test; it does not run in CI until 299 lands.
root_cause: The constraints/orient/review MCP handlers evaluated DD-backed constraints without holding the parse-coordinator lock that the reparse action holds. evaluate_dd reads files (path_map), components and import edges across three separate Mutex<Connection> acquisitions with no single transaction; Db::replace_file_data remints file ids (AUTOINCREMENT delete+reinsert) and commits per file. So a reparse committing between the all_files() read and the import_edges() read paired an old-id path_map with new-id edges — the same disjoint-id space that produced silent-clean results in sutra/297, here opened by endpoint/reparse concurrency rather than a stale cached graph.

messages.author: agent
messages.text:
Implemented the read-side generation guard: `evaluate()`'s DdBacked arm now reads `data_generation` before and after `evaluate_dd`, returns the result only if it was stable, retries (up to 4×) otherwise, and returns an explicit Internal error on sustained churn. Compiles; all 57 existing constraint tests pass unchanged.

BUT while writing the concurrent regression test I discovered a bigger problem, filed as sutra/299: driving the shared DdEngine concurrently with a file-id-reminting reparse HANGS (~30% of runs) — the reparse thread spins in an unbounded SQLite write loop. It's pre-existing (reproduces with the pre-guard single-shot evaluate) and only appears when the DdEngine is present (a Db-only two-thread hammer is clean 15/15).

Implication for THIS task: the generation guard detects an incoherent read and retries, but each retry re-drives the engine — so under a genuinely concurrent reparse the guard does NOT prevent the sutra/299 hang; it may even amplify it. The robust fix for the 298 coherence gap is probably to SERIALIZE evaluation against reparse: have the constraint/orient endpoints acquire the parse-coordinator lock the reparse action already holds (Codex's alternative). That closes both the silent-clean and the hang windows. The read-side guard is then cheap belt-and-suspenders, not the primary fix.

Status: guard code is in place and green on sequential tests; the concurrent regression test is currently removed/quarantined because it trips sutra/299. Paused for a direction call on guard-only vs endpoint-serialization before proceeding.
